items.text: Nine painted lady pupae, scanned alive by X-ray computed tomography through their pupal days, have most of the adult tracheal system formed from the first day of pupation. Their larval midgut, whole on day 1, reaches its final position by day 7. Several of the pupae hatch after repeated scans. Muscle and the central nervous system go unresolved in these scans, for lack of contrast. Tobacco hornworm moth larvae given the odour of ethyl acetate with an electric shock at their fifth larval stage grow into adults, 77 per cent of which choose plain air over the odour (27 adults, p = 0.005). Adults from larvae trained at the third stage (15 adults), and adults from larvae given the odour alone or the shock alone, avoid it at an empty set.
